subject.title: fix(codex): bound app-server websocket handshake waits at 30s

question: Should Codex app-server TCP and Unix WebSocket upgrades both adopt an unconditional 30-second handshake deadline?
rationale: Source and proof establish the indefinite-wait bug, but repository behavior does not establish whether accepted connections that upgrade after 30 seconds are unsupported; that compatibility boundary requires Codex-owner intent.

options.title: Confirm 30 seconds and merge
options.body: Accept the shared fixed deadline because app-server upgrades should complete promptly and stalled peers must terminate predictably.

options.title: Reuse an existing lifecycle budget
options.body: Derive the handshake deadline from an existing app-server request or startup budget if maintainers need deployments with longer accepted upgrade delays.

options.title: Pause the deadline change
options.body: Keep the current behavior until Codex defines a supported upgrade deadline or a broader connection-lifecycle policy.

recommendation.title: Confirm 30 seconds and merge
recommendation.body: Accept the shared fixed deadline because app-server upgrades should complete promptly and stalled peers must terminate predictably.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Codex app-server integration and configuration history makes this person the strongest available decision owner.
